topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, student backgrounds, and core learning outcomes for the cancer biology module.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer and modeling challenges
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through genetic and epigenetic disruptions to normal differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture, addressing how experimental models capture these changes.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign versus malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological, gross, and histological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on mechanisms of invasion, metastasis, and stepwise tissue progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification rules
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and notable exceptions used to classify and name tumors according to tissue of origin and malignant potential.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the local, structural, and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors impair physiological function to cause illness and death.

topics.label: Patterns of tumor incidence across humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the incidence and epidemiological distribution of benign and malignant tumors across human populations and throughout multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, histological basis, and practical efficacy of screening methods used to detect tumors before they become invasive.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap of learning outcomes and reminders for upcoming practicals and lectures.
